title: fix(linux): keep Quick Chat widgets bound to their Gateway
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145355

Stack 5/8, replayed onto main after the Quick Chat recovery layer landed.
Previous: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146048 | Next: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/146050

This same-repository branch is writable by maintainers with push access.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes retained Quick Chat widgets using a replacement Gateway's access and slow widget updates accumulating obsolete pending state.

## User Impact

Widgets stay bound to their owning Gateway. Reconnecting to that same owner can refresh access; replacing the Gateway cannot transfer access to old previews. Slow synchronization converges on the latest layout without an unbounded backlog.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move Canvas generation and observed-URL ownership through native commands and renderer callers together. Recheck that authority when creating or showing a child on the native UI thread. Keep one active widget update and only the latest pending update.

The replay retains the landed socket configuration/generation guards, independent desktop requests and sleep ownership. Existing window chrome and publication documentation remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Current replay: 37 renderer tests passed, including owner replacement, same-owner reconnect, stale refresh completion, coalesced layout/clear/hide transitions and current versus superseded failures. Targeted TypeScript lint/format and JavaScript syntax passed.
- Source composition: the native widget and renderer files match the reviewed original layer. Canvas requests use the existing dispatcher; the malformed-response test retains its all-platform configuration constructor. Native signatures, serialized state, commands and renderer callers move together.
- Reused aggregate proof includes the intended original coalescing failures and the retained native widget owner flow. This is historical behavior evidence, not a new GUI execution of this replay.
- Fresh scoped composition review through P2 completed with no findings and final source verification. Signed replay `e0b55c7b0e04bcf4ead26ed09f44c3cd7b8a19a2` has the exact reviewed and natively tested tree. The investigated main sync `a8a43c406e1bc5dca7b88b4eae8916106d9c92de` preserves its full five-file delta byte-for-byte while inheriting the upstream QA repair and unrelated platform-copy changes.
- [Recorded native task](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34774489812): Rust 1.98.1 formatting and native build passed; Gateway owner tests passed 39, widget owner tests passed 5. Each suite intentionally ignored one isolated-display test; neither is counted as passing. Source pins matched before/after, and the task was stopped after retention. This is owner/build proof, not a fresh native GUI or cross-platform run.
- [LinuxApp on the current head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34778351808) passed Linux formatting, Rust tests/build, native inline-browser behavior and the macOS companion. Packaging and packaged first-run were skipped. [Current-head core CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34778351804) completed successfully; both runs bind `a8a43c406e1bc5dca7b88b4eae8916106d9c92de`.
- [Core CI on the pre-sync head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34775163935) failed an inherited QA Profile Evidence routing expectation: the main merge added a valid sixth test target while the expectation still listed five. The Linux delta changes neither the routing owner nor its inputs. Upstream [#147293](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147293) repaired that expectation; this head includes it without adding a Linux-owned CI fix or relaxing a check.
- The widget-specific before/after images below were serially inspected and are privacy-clean. They show preserved rendering in a native Tauri/GTK widget-owner fixture with a synthetic parent and HTML. They are not full Quick Chat, race-behavior or normal-Quit proof. Historical Quick Chat recovery captures are not substitutes.

### Native Widget Rendering

Before:

![Before: synthetic native Tauri/GTK widget-owner fixture](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd7dd1a3-b721-492b-a85b-a79a4f33dca3)

After:

![After: preserved rendering in the synthetic native Tauri/GTK widget-owner fixture](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae2eccfd-f689-48b4-8e0c-1cf03b05bd6b)

Both embedded images were verified visibly rendering in this GitHub PR during
[isolated browser proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34783370131).
Both images also render in the originating chat, explicitly confirmed by the
requester. Screenshot delivery to both destinations is complete. Current-head
core and LinuxApp CI are green; the PR is ready for native landing checks.

No new widget feature, dependency, default-graphics/Wayland qualification, packaged-install proof or performance claim is introduced.
